analyst_view.overall: Manchester City are 7th on 9 points but come in on four Premier League games without a win after Saturday's 1-1 home draw with Fulham. Enzo Maresca is missing only Semenyo (already in the numbers); Matheus Nunes is a doubt, Khusanov played through a knock and Enzo Fernandez should return to midfield. Napoli, 27th on 3 points, travel without eleven players: Buongiorno, Neres, Vergara (new thigh injury against Torino) and the suspended Rafa Marin are out on top of Lobotka, Di Lorenzo, Meret, Badiashile and Alisson Santos, which leaves Allegri with only Beukema and Rrahmani as real centre-backs and Olivera filling in. The numbers count Lobotka and Di Lorenzo but not Buongiorno, Rafa Marin, Neres or Vergara, and Allegri has said Napoli's campaign will be decided in the games against Club Brugge, Sabah and Viking. Romanian referee Istvan Kovacs has been appointed; the numbers had no referee on file.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals and already take off for Semenyo, Di Lorenzo and Lobotka. What they do not know is that Napoli are also without Buongiorno and the suspended Rafa Marin, so a makeshift back line with Olivera at centre-back faces City at the Etihad, while De Bruyne and Hojlund still give Napoli a way to score against a City side that has not kept a clean sheet in weeks. That is a clear reason to go up: 3.3 x 1.06, about 3.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, mostly City's (about 6.7), and already add about 10% for how many corners Napoli have conceded lately. With a patched-up defence and Allegri likely to sit in a back five, Napoli should be pinned back even more than their record shows, and blocked crosses and shots turn into corners. A mild lean up, to about 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, with Napoli's busier recent card count included (+12%), but they had no referee on file. Istvan Kovacs, who has been appointed, averages close to four yellows a game in his recent international matches, and a stand-in Napoli defence chasing Doku and City's wingers is likely to give away fouls. A mild lean up, to about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.6 shots and already add about 13% to City for the volume Napoli have been allowing. Napoli's extra absences at the back (Buongiorno, Rafa Marin) and up front (Vergara, Neres) are not in that figure and point to City having even more of the ball and Napoli fewer outlets. I go up to 28.6 x 1.05, about 30.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, with Napoli's sharp recent finishing (+8%) already counted. A weakened Napoli back line should let City get more of their shots away from closer in, though City managed only three on target against Fulham, so I keep the move moderate: 10.4 x 1.05, about 10.9.
